messages:
amelia: quick copy review — revoking an API key for service accounts. worried current modal doesn't sufficiently warn about downstream breakage. dropping it here before i update figma.

amelia: Current copy:
Title: Revoke API key?
Body: Revoking this key will stop access immediately.
Primary: Revoke
Secondary: Cancel

amelia: problems: generic verb 'Revoke' on its own is terse; users may not realize this affects cron jobs, integrations, and dashboards. also need to surface who issued the key (service account vs user) and suggest safer alternatives like rotating keys or deactivating first.

pranav: +1. We should use explicit noun in CTA: 'Revoke key' or 'Deactivate key' depending on the action. If we have soft-deactivate, prefer that wording. Also show last used timestamp and a list of dependent resources if available.

pranav: copy idea (permanent):
Title: Revoke API key
Body: Revoking this API key will immediately stop access for any services that use it (cron jobs, integrations, dashboards). This cannot be undone.
Primary: Revoke API key
Secondary: Cancel

jordan: i like calling out examples (cron jobs, integrations). consider offering a quick checklist line: 'Tip: rotate the key instead to avoid downtime.' and link to docs. Tone: firm but not scary.

sam: accessibility + usability: primary button should include the key name or id for context (e.g., 'Revoke key: deploy-service-sa'). avoid using only color to indicate danger; include an icon and aria-describedby for the irreversible line. For service accounts we should add 'Issued to: <service account name>' in the modal body.

aria-bot: a11y checklist: focus should move to modal heading; ensure role=dialog and aria-modal="true"; avoid relying on color; provide keyboard confirmation patterns. For destructive actions add a typed confirmation for highly privileged keys (e.g., type the key name) if the key has admin scopes.

amelia: proposal combining safety + clarity:

Title: Revoke API key
Body: This will immediately revoke access for any services using this key (cron jobs, integrations, dashboards). Issued to: deploy-service-sa. If you're unsure, consider rotating or deactivating the key instead. Revoking cannot be undone.
Primary: Revoke key
Secondary: Deactivate instead

amelia: for very high-impact keys we can add a small input: 'Type the key name to confirm: <key-id>' and change primary to 'Confirm revoke'. Only enable that for admin-scoped keys.

pranav: nit: 'Deactivate instead' sounds like an action the secondary button triggers. Is the pattern that secondary performs a non-destructive alternative? Should we instead have a tertiary action or a link 'Deactivate' that opens the deactivate flow?

jordan: good point. i prefer secondary to be 'Cancel' and add a plaintext link 'Rotate or deactivate' below the primary CTAs. keeps button semantics clear.

sam: agree. buttons should be consistent. also add analytics tag data-action:revoke_key so we can track accidental revokes. and aria-label on primary: 'Revoke API key deploy-service-sa'.

amelia: updated copy then:

Title: Revoke API key
Body: This will immediately revoke access for any services using this key (cron jobs, integrations, dashboards). Issued to: deploy-service-sa. If you're unsure, rotate or deactivate the key instead. Revoking cannot be undone.
Primary: Revoke key
Secondary: Cancel
Link (small): Rotate or deactivate key

amelia: i'll update Figma with the variant that includes typed confirmation for admin keys and add the aria-label and analytics hooks. tagging PM for approval.

pranav: :thumbsup: make sure copy uses sentence case and punctuation matches our modal pattern.

jordan: also check localization edge cases — key names with special characters in confirmation inputs.

sam: i'll add a dev note: aria-live for status updates and ensure we surface last-used timestamp if available.

amelia: perfect. unless objections i'll land this and open the copy ticket. thanks all! :sparkles:
